messages:
Mira Patel: Heads-up — we're seeing repeated ECC/Xid errors on a subset of NVidia cards in the eu-west-1 Dedicated pool (nodes gpu-03, gpu-07). I'm starting a drain/replace for affected hosts. Need customer-facing comms for any Dedicated/Private customers that might see failovers.

Samir Rao: TL;DR: hardware fault pattern, increasing soft ECC then occasional Xid 31/43 spikes. We validated kernel logs and NVML counters. Counts: ~120 ECC events last 24h on gpu-03, rising.

Samir Rao: Mitigations in flight: marking nodes cordoned, rolling live drains, triggering spare allocations. No data plane loss but some sessions were moved -> short re-connections.

deploy-bot: [action] cordon gpu-03 at 2024-11-05T21:10Z
deploy-bot: [action] drain initiated on gpu-03 - 12 active tasks migrated

Jordan Lee: Thanks. For customer messaging we should be explicit about: what happened, who is affected, what we're doing, expected impact, ETA for replacement, and contact for escalation. Keep it concise.

Evelyn (CSM): Here's a short draft for affected Dedicated customers (can paste to support cases):

```
Hi <CustomerName>,

We wanted to let you know we detected intermittent GPU memory ECC errors and corresponding Xid events on a host serving your Dedicated capacity in eu-west-1. To prevent customer impact we've initiated a live drain of the host and are replacing the underlying GPU.

What you may see: a small number of short reconnects for some in-flight requests and brief increases in latency while requests are re-routed. We do not expect request loss or data leakage.

What we're doing: cordoning the host, migrating workloads to spare capacity, and provisioning a replacement GPU. Replacement is scheduled within the next 6 hours; the live drain should complete within ~30–90 minutes.

If you'd like us to schedule a maintenance window or pause automatic failovers while you test, reply and we'll coordinate.

Sincerely,
The Redwood Inference Operations Team
```

Jordan Lee: For Private (VPC) customers we need an ops-level alternative message — sounds like they may prefer opt-in replacement windows. Suggest adding: "If you require an on-prem or VPC-hosted replacement to be scheduled during a maintenance window, tell us preferred windows and we'll book a technician."

Mira Patel: Also include a short note about mitigation steps we already took (cordon/drain) and an internal contact alias (cc: infra-dedicated@redwood.ai).

Samir Rao: ETA update: vendor confirmed a replacement GPU shipment and remote swap is scheduled for 2024-11-06 03:00-05:00 UTC. If hardware swap goes as planned we expect no more than a 10–15 minute control-plane pause for that host; live drains address in-flight requests.

Evelyn (CSM): Added a shorter push-notification style blurb for customers in the console: "We're replacing a GPU in your Dedicated pool in eu-west-1. You may see short reconnects or slight latency — our team is on it. Contact your CSM for questions."

Ops SRE: Quick note for SRE docs: track affected host IDs, ECC count, vendor RMA ID, and mark as warranty swap. Also create a follow-up postmortem if we hit >3 customer-impacting events.

Mira Patel: Ask: please review the draft and approve sending at 2024-11-05 18:00 UTC, or propose edits. If no objections by +2h we'll start sending to impacted customers and raise support cases for Private customers requiring manual windows.

Jordan Lee: Approved from product/CS — small edit: change "no more than a 10–15 minute control-plane pause" -> "we expect any control-plane pause to be brief (typically under 10 minutes)".

Samir Rao: Noted. Also adding optional workaround: pin customers that must avoid live migration to a warm spare (cost impact) — can propose as an opt-in in the support case.

Evelyn (CSM): Sending final copy to support queue now. Will include a link to the status page and the incident tag. :thumbsup:

Mira Patel: Thanks all. I'll follow up with the replacement confirmation and the post-swap verification checklist (memory/temperature/latency baseline).

Jordan Lee: One last ask — can eng-sre run an automated check to flag any card with >50 ECC events in 24h so we can preempt next time?

Samir Rao: Yes, will add a short rule to fleet-monitoring and tune thresholds.

Mira Patel: Closing thread — sending at 18:00 UTC as planned.
